title: Zechariah Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Zechariah chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Zechariah Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Zechariah Chapter 11.

questions.question: In Zechariah 11, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Feed the flock of the slaughter
questions.explanation: This is the first command given in the chapter, found in Zechariah 11:1.

questions.question: What does the LORD command regarding the flock?
options: Feed the flock of the slaughter
questions.correctAnswer: Feed the flock of the slaughter
questions.explanation: The LORD directly instructs to 'Feed the flock of the slaughter' in Zechariah 11:4.

questions.question: What should the fir tree do according to Zechariah 11:2?
questions.explanation: The fir tree is instructed to 'Howl' because the cedar has fallen in Zechariah 11:2.

questions.question: What is the condition of the shepherds in Zechariah 11:3?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'their glory is spoiled' in Zechariah 11:3.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 11:5, how do the possessors treat the flock?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that 'Whose possessors slay them' in Zechariah 11:5.

questions.question: What do the sellers say in Zechariah 11:5?
options: Blessed be the LORD; for I am rich
questions.correctAnswer: Blessed be the LORD; for I am rich
questions.explanation: This phrase is directly quoted in Zechariah 11:5.

questions.question: What will the LORD no longer do to the inhabitants of the land according to Zechariah 11:6?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'For I will no more pity the inhabitants of the land' in Zechariah 11:6.

questions.question: Who will deliver the men into the hands of their neighbors according to Zechariah 11:6?
questions.explanation: The LORD declares that He will deliver them in Zechariah 11:6.

questions.question: What is spoiled according to Zechariah 11:3?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that 'the pride of Jordan is spoiled' in Zechariah 11:3.

questions.question: What type of tree is mentioned along with the cedar in Zechariah 11:2?
questions.explanation: The oaks of Bashan are mentioned in Zechariah 11:2.

questions.question: What is happening to the land according to Zechariah 11:6?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that 'they shall smite the land' in Zechariah 11:6.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD asks Lebanon to open its doors.
questions.explanation: The LORD commands Lebanon to 'Open thy doors' in Zechariah 11:1.

questions.question: True or False: The young lions are roaring because of the glory of the shepherds.
questions.explanation: The text states there is a voice of the roaring of young lions because 'their glory is spoiled' in Zechariah 11:3.

questions.question: True or False: The inhabitants of the land will be saved by the LORD.
questions.explanation: The text states that the LORD will no more pity them and will deliver them into the hands of others in Zechariah 11:6.

questions.question: True or False: The shepherds pity the flock according to Zechariah 11:5.
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'their own shepherds pity them not' in Zechariah 11:5.

medium.title: Zechariah Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Zechariah Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What two staves did Zechariah take to feed the flock?
questions.explanation: This is correct as stated in Zechariah 11:7, where it mentions that he took two staves and named them Beauty and Bands.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 11:4 promise will happen if someone feeds the flock of slaughter?
questions.explanation: Feeding the flock of slaughter is an act of obedience to God's command, and it aligns with His promise of support and blessing.

questions.question: How did Zechariah feel about the three shepherds he cut off?
questions.explanation: This is accurate as stated in Zechariah 11:8, where it explicitly mentions that his soul loathed them.

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned in Zechariah 11:9 for not feeding the flock?
options: They will turn on each other
questions.correctAnswer: They will turn on each other
questions.explanation: This reflects the dire situation described in Zechariah 11:9, where it states that the ones remaining will eat each other's flesh.

questions.question: What action did Zechariah take with the staff named Beauty?
questions.explanation: According to Zechariah 11:10, he took the staff named Beauty and cut it asunder, which symbolizes the breaking of the covenant.

questions.question: What did the poor of the flock understand in Zechariah 11:11?
options: That it was a time of joy
That it was the word of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: That it was the word of the LORD
questions.explanation: This is confirmed in Zechariah 11:11, where it states that the poor of the flock knew it was the word of the LORD when the covenant was broken.

questions.question: What price was weighed for Zechariah in Zechariah 11:12?
questions.explanation: This is indicated in Zechariah 11:12, where it states that they weighed thirty pieces of silver for his price.

questions.question: What do the shepherds do according to Zechariah 11:5?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:5 describes how the possessors slay the flock and feel no guilt, highlighting the failure of the shepherds.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 11:6 indicate about God's feelings towards the inhabitants of the land?
options: He will no more pity them
questions.correctAnswer: He will no more pity them
questions.explanation: This is stated in Zechariah 11:6, where God declares He will no more have pity on the inhabitants of the land.

questions.question: What event does Zechariah 11:3 describe regarding the shepherds?
questions.explanation: The verse Zechariah 11:3 describes a voice of the howling of the shepherds, indicating that their glory has been spoiled.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 11:2, what is happening to the mighty?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:2 states that the cedar is fallen, indicating the downfall of the mighty.

questions.question: The statement 'let the rest eat every one the flesh of another' implies what about the flock's condition?
questions.explanation: This statement from Zechariah 11:9 reflects a desperate and cannibalistic situation, indicating severe despair among the flock.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah took only one staff to feed the flock.
questions.explanation: This is false as Zechariah took two staves, named Beauty and Bands, as stated in Zechariah 11:7.

questions.question: True or False: The flock of slaughter is described as being well cared for.
questions.explanation: This is false as the flock of slaughter is described as neglected and doomed in the context of Zechariah 11:5.

questions.question: True or False: God broke his covenant with the people according to Zechariah 11:10.
questions.explanation: This statement is true as Zechariah 11:10 says that he broke the covenant made with all the people.

hard.title: Zechariah Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Zechariah Chapter 11.

questions.question: In Zechariah 11:13, what was done with the thirty pieces of silver?
options: Cast them to the potter in the house of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Cast them to the potter in the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:13 explicitly states that the thirty pieces of silver were cast to the potter in the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What was the symbolic meaning of cutting asunder the staff called Bands in Zechariah 11:14?
options: To break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel
To signify the covenant with the people
questions.correctAnswer: To break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:14 states that cutting asunder the staff called Bands was done to break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 11:15, what instruments was the prophet commanded to take?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:15 states that the LORD told the prophet to take instruments of a foolish shepherd.

questions.question: In Zechariah 11:16, which characteristic is NOT attributed to the shepherd that will be raised up?
options: He shall heal that that is broken
He shall not visit those that be cut off
He shall not seek the young one
He shall eat the flesh of the fat
questions.correctAnswer: He shall heal that that is broken
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:16 clearly describes the shepherd as one who will NOT heal that that is broken, indicating neglect rather than care.

questions.question: What is the woe pronounced on the idol shepherd in Zechariah 11:17?
options: The sword shall be upon his arm and his right eye, his arm dried up and his right eye darkened
He shall be exalted among the nations
He shall bring peace to the flock
He shall prosper and reign forever
questions.correctAnswer: The sword shall be upon his arm and his right eye, his arm dried up and his right eye darkened
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:17 pronounces woe on the idol shepherd with the sword upon his arm and right eye, with his arm dried up and eye darkened.

questions.question: Why did the LORD say to cast the thirty pieces of silver to the potter according to Zechariah 11:13?
options: It was a goodly price at which He was prized by them
questions.correctAnswer: It was a goodly price at which He was prized by them
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:13 states the thirty pieces of silver was 'a goodly price that I was prised at of them,' indicating mockery of His value.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'ro’eh' (רֹעֶה) in Zechariah 11:4 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'ro’eh' in Zechariah 11:4 translates as 'shepherd,' referring to one who tends a flock.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Zechariah 11:7–14, involving the two staves named Beauty and Bands?
questions.explanation: The two staves Beauty and Bands symbolize covenant and unity, a clear example of symbolism in Zechariah 11:7–14.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects to the theme of the thirty pieces of silver found in Zechariah 11:12-13?
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:9-10 quotes the thirty pieces of silver price and casting to the potter, directly connecting to Zechariah 11:12-13.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of a foolish shepherd neglecting the flock as in Zechariah 11:16-17?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:2-6 condemns shepherds who neglect the flock, echoing Zechariah 11:16-17's theme of a foolish shepherd.

questions.question: What action directly precedes the casting of thirty pieces of silver in Zechariah 11?
options: The people weighing out thirty pieces of silver as his price
The cutting of the staff called Beauty
The woe against the idol shepherd
The taking of instruments of a foolish shepherd
questions.correctAnswer: The people weighing out thirty pieces of silver as his price
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:12 describes the people weighing out thirty pieces of silver before the casting in verse 13.

questions.question: What type of foreshadowing is present in Zechariah 11:13 regarding the thirty pieces of silver?
options: Messianic foreshadowing of Judas' betrayal price
Foreshadowing of the destruction of Jerusalem
Foreshadowing of the coming of Elijah
questions.correctAnswer: Messianic foreshadowing of Judas' betrayal price
questions.explanation: The thirty pieces of silver in Zechariah 11:13 foreshadow the price Judas received for betraying Jesus, as detailed in Matthew 26:15.

questions.question: How does the cutting of the staff named Beauty in Zechariah 11:10 serve as an inclusio in the chapter?
options: It frames the breaking of covenant theme from beginning to end
It introduces the idea of restoration
It signals the start of a new covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It frames the breaking of covenant theme from beginning to end
questions.explanation: Cutting the staff Beauty in Zechariah 11:10 marks breaking the covenant, which frames the chapter's themes of judgment and broken relationships.

questions.question: Does Zechariah 11:6 indicate that the LORD will no longer have pity on the inhabitants of the land?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:6 states, 'For I will no more pity the inhabitants of the land,' confirming the LORD's withdrawal of pity.

questions.question: Is it true that in Zechariah 11:9 the prophet declares he will continue to feed the flock with care and compassion?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:9 states the prophet will no longer feed the flock, letting the dying die and the rest eat each other, showing lack of care.

theological.title: Zechariah Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Zechariah Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Zechariah 11:6 teach about God's nature in relation to judgment and human sin?
options: God’s patience leads Him to indefinitely withhold judgment
God delivers sinners into the hands of their oppressors as a form of judgment
God ignores human sin and allows evil to prosper unchallenged
God immediately destroys sinners without any warning
questions.correctAnswer: God delivers sinners into the hands of their oppressors as a form of judgment
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:6 states that the LORD will deliver men into the hand of their neighbor and king, signifying a judicial handing over due to their sinfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine about covenant faithfulness does Zechariah 11:10 teach?
options: God’s covenants are eternal and unbreakable under all circumstances
The breaking of a covenant can symbolize judgment and severance of relationship
Covenants are human agreements without divine significance
God’s covenant blessings are unconditional regardless of human response
questions.correctAnswer: The breaking of a covenant can symbolize judgment and severance of relationship
questions.explanation: In Zechariah 11:10, breaking the staff named Beauty symbolizes breaking the covenant with the people, indicating God’s judgment and covenantal severance.

questions.question: What doctrine about false leadership and its consequences does Zechariah 11:16 teach?
options: False shepherds care only for the weak and broken
False shepherds neglect the vulnerable and exploit the strong
True shepherds exploit the flock for personal gain
All shepherds are ultimately faithful and protective
questions.correctAnswer: False shepherds neglect the vulnerable and exploit the strong
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:16 describes a shepherd who does not care for the cut off or broken but eats the flesh of the fat, illustrating neglect of the weak and exploitation of the strong.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Zechariah 11:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:4 shows the LORD’s sovereign command to feed the flock of the slaughter, demonstrating His authority over circumstances and people.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Zechariah 11:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:7 shows God feeding the flock despite their unworthiness, indicating His patience and longsuffering toward His people.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 11 connect to the theme of rejected Messiahship in the New Testament?
options: It predicts the Messiah’s triumphant earthly reign without opposition
It symbolizes the rejection and betrayal of the Messiah by His own people
It emphasizes the Messiah’s divine nature without human suffering
It focuses exclusively on Israel’s national restoration without messianic implications
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the rejection and betrayal of the Messiah by His own people
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:12-13, where the shepherd is paid thirty pieces of silver and the price is cast to the potter, is a prophetic type fulfilled in the betrayal of Jesus Christ (Matthew 26:15, 27:9).

questions.question: How does the breaking of the two staffs in Zechariah 11:10 and 11:14 prepare for themes of division and judgment in later Scripture?
options: It foreshadows the permanent unity of Israel and Judah
It symbolizes the breaking of covenant and the division between Israel and Judah
It indicates God’s abandonment of all His promises forever
It foretells peace and reconciliation between all nations
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the breaking of covenant and the division between Israel and Judah
questions.explanation: The cutting of the staff Beauty breaks the covenant (v.10), and cutting Bands breaks brotherhood between Judah and Israel (v.14), pointing to national division and judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Zechariah 11:4 and 11:5 teach about God’s judgment on human sin and the role of leaders?
options: God ignores sinful leaders and allows them to prosper
God holds leaders accountable for abusing their flock and punishes them
God rewards corrupt leaders for their wealth
God’s judgment is unrelated to leadership or sin
questions.correctAnswer: God holds leaders accountable for abusing their flock and punishes them
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:4 commands feeding the slaughtered flock, while 11:5 condemns the shepherds who kill and sell the flock without pity, highlighting divine judgment on corrupt leadership.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Zechariah 11:12 and 11:13 teach about the value of Christ’s betrayal and its theological significance?
options: The price paid for Christ was insignificant and without meaning
The thirty pieces of silver represent the rejection and undervaluing of the Messiah
The betrayal was a mistake without divine purpose
The price signifies God’s approval of the betrayal
questions.correctAnswer: The thirty pieces of silver represent the rejection and undervaluing of the Messiah
questions.explanation: Verses 12 and 13 show the shepherd’s price weighed out at thirty pieces of silver and cast to the potter, symbolizing the Messiah’s rejection and the valuation of His life by His people.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Zechariah 11:16 and 11:17 teach about false shepherds and divine judgment?
options: False shepherds will be exalted and blessed by God
False shepherds neglect their duties and will suffer divine punishment
False shepherds are immune to judgment due to their position
False shepherds are commended for their zeal
questions.correctAnswer: False shepherds neglect their duties and will suffer divine punishment
questions.explanation: Verse 16 describes a shepherd who neglects the weak and preys on the strong, and verse 17 pronounces woe and specific divine judgment on such an idol shepherd.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Zechariah 11:7-9 teaches that God is indifferent to the suffering of His people. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God abandons the flock without care or concern
God initially feeds the flock but then withdraws pity due to their rebellion
God’s lack of pity means He does not love His people
God’s actions show randomness without purpose
questions.correctAnswer: God initially feeds the flock but then withdraws pity due to their rebellion
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:7-9 shows God feeding the poor flock but then deciding not to feed them anymore, reflecting judgment in response to persistent sin, not indifference.

questions.question: What doctrine about human pride and divine judgment is taught in Zechariah 11:2?
options: Human pride leads to divine blessing
The mighty and proud will be brought low by God’s judgment
Pride is rewarded with lasting security
questions.correctAnswer: The mighty and proud will be brought low by God’s judgment
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:2 mourns the fall of the mighty cedars and oaks, symbolizing that God will humble the proud and powerful.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Zechariah 11:13 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Casting the thirty pieces of silver to the potter (v.13) shows God’s just response to the price set on His servant, reflecting divine justice against betrayal.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s use of symbols and prophetic actions is taught in Zechariah 11:14?
options: God never uses symbolic acts to communicate
God uses symbolic acts, such as breaking a staff, to signify covenant and relational changes
Symbolic acts are human inventions without divine meaning
Prophetic symbolism is always literal and never figurative
questions.correctAnswer: God uses symbolic acts, such as breaking a staff, to signify covenant and relational changes
questions.explanation: Zechariah 11:14 describes cutting the staff Bands to break brotherhood, highlighting God’s use of symbolic prophetic actions to communicate judgment.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 11:1 contribute to the overarching biblical theme of divine judgment on creation?
options: It portrays God as indifferent to natural disasters
It depicts God actively using natural elements to carry out judgment
It shows creation as independent from God’s will
It denies any connection between nature and divine action
questions.correctAnswer: It depicts God actively using natural elements to carry out judgment
questions.explanation: Opening the doors of Lebanon for fire to devour cedars (v.1) illustrates God’s sovereign control over nature to execute judgment.
